name: How long does a small multifamily project take from feasibility to completion in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How long does it usually take to build a duplex, triplex, or small apartment building in Los Angeles from initial site review to final inspection?
mainEntity.text: How long does it usually take to build a duplex, triplex, or small apartment building in Los Angeles from initial site review to final inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small multifamily project in Los Angeles typically runs on a multi-phase timeline rather than a single construction schedule. Design and feasibility may take 1 to 3 months, permit-ready drawings another few months, and permitting can stretch if the site has zoning complications, hillside conditions, parking issues, or agency comments. Construction itself may be 6 to 12 months for a modest duplex, triplex, or small apartment building, but overall delivery often lands closer to 6 to 18 months and can extend beyond that when approvals are complex. The biggest timeline variables are plan check revisions, demolition or utility relocation, lender requirements, and whether the project is standard or has bonus or variance-related review. Owners should ask for a schedule that separates preconstruction, permitting, and field work so delays are easier to identify early. A realistic contractor should also flag long-lead items such as windows, switchgear, and custom finishes before construction starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: A small multifamily project in Los Angeles often takes about 6 to 18 months from design through construction, but the full timeline can be longer once feasibility, permitting, utility coordination, and plan revisions are included. Site constraints, zoning, parking, and approval review cycles can add months. Fast-track projects with clean entitlements move sooner.
